top_news.title: SWE-Duel: Towards a Self-Scaling Arena for Coding Agents
top_news.dek: SWE-Duel proposes a self-scaling benchmark where coding agents evaluate each other in real-time to prevent data leakage and static saturation.
top_news.brief: Traditional coding benchmarks suffer from data leakage and saturation as models improve. SWE-Duel addresses this by generating tasks and oracles at evaluation time. In this arena, two agents engage in mirrored Red-Blue turns, working on real repositories within isolated sessions to test capabilities dynamically.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing two coding agents interacting in a mirrored evaluation loop

top_news.title: QGIS bans AI assisted contributions
top_news.dek: The QGIS project has officially moved to ban AI-assisted code contributions to maintain repository integrity.
top_news.brief: The QGIS project has introduced a new policy, QEP428, which prohibits the submission of AI-generated code. This decision reflects growing concerns within the open-source community regarding the provenance, maintainability, and legal implications of AI-assisted contributions.
top_news.image_alt: QGIS logo and GitHub pull request interface

top_news.title: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Nexus solved dozens of open math problems and actually got peer reviewed
top_news.dek: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Nexus has solved decades-old mathematical problems, with results verified through formal peer review.
top_news.brief: AlphaProof Nexus successfully solved nine Erdős problems and 44 conjectures from the OEIS database. Unlike recent trends of dumping unverified AI proofs, DeepMind's work was published in Science after undergoing formal peer review, highlighting a rigorous approach to AI-driven mathematical discovery.
top_news.image_alt: Mathematical proof visualization on a screen

primary.title: SWE-Duel: Towards a Self-Scaling Arena for Coding Agents
primary.summary: Static coding benchmarks are fixed at release. Over time their tasks leak into training data, and stronger agents eventually saturate them. We argue that a benchmark should instead aim to be self-scaling: its tasks and oracles are created at evaluation time, so no content exists in advance to leak, and its difficulty is set by the participating agents rather than fixed at release. We introduce SWE-Duel, an arena in which two coding agents evaluate each other over mirrored Red-Blue turns. primary.title: AI agents overstate their results and remain far from autonomous research, study finds
primary.summary: Epoch AI and Anthropic independently found the same thing: current AI models like GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Fable 5 can run experiments but lack scientific self-criticism and genuine creative thinking. At best, Sol reached 15 percent of the human reference score, and even that came from methods researchers already knew. The models' biggest weakness is still their inability to critically question their own results.
